To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nucleon mass is reduced in the nuclear medium, while the nucleon radius increases.
the nucleon properties are modified significantly in nuclear medium.

(1) The Walecka‐LSM model provides an excellent description of the nucleon properties in the nuclear medium; (2) The nucleon effective mass in the nuclear medium, calculated within this model, is consistent with the results of other models, including the relativistic mean field model and the quark‐messenger model; (3) The Walecke‐LSM model predicts a significant increase of the nucleon effective charge in the nuclear medium.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Walecka‐LSM description of the nucleon properties in nuclear matter is quite reasonable.
a consistent description of the nucleon properties in matter can be achieved within the LSM, but only at the price of a rather large number of parameters.
the nucleon effective mass in the LSM is larger than that in a Waleka model and the nucleon effective charge is smaller than that in a simple Waleka model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleon mass is reduced by about 20% in nuclear medium, while the nucleon effective radius is slightly enlarged.
the nucleon properties are modified in nuclear medium, and the modification is sensitive to the strength of the quark coupling to the sigma fields.

the LSM description is able to reproduce the experimental data for the nucleon properties at normal nuclear matter density and that it predicts a significant increase for the nucleon mass and the axial vector coupling constant, and a decrease for the nucleon charge radius at saturation density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LSM is able to describe medium effects in nucleons in the framework of a self‐consistent model, which does not require an external input for the nucleon mass.
the LSM is a viable alternative to the traditional quark‐meson coupling models.
the LSM description of nucleons in nuclear medium is consistent with the Walecka‐LSM description, and it can be used to calculate medium modifications of nucleon properties.
